D1 research authoring, batch 82 (2026-09-27): one ASSOCIATION_ONLY draft mapping added at rank 1 (colorectal-cancer) pending qualified-human citation verification under docs/citation-verification-sop.md; mapping approval is not citation verification. This is the smallest authored file in batch 82 by design: seborrhoeic keratosis is a benign epithelial tumour whose clinically important association is a paraneoplastic signal rather than a set of sequelae, and the located evidence is case-report class only, so a single edge is the honest ceiling rather than a shortfall.

Classification and mechanism-vocabulary guard: the single edge asserts association only (etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true) at MALIGNANT_TRANSFORMATION. That category is the closest available term in the controlled vocabulary, but the located evidence describes a PARANEOPLASTIC SIGNALLING route and not transformation of a keratosis, and the mismatch is disclosed on the face of the edge rather than resolved by inventing a category outside the vocabulary. A reviewing clinician must treat the mechanism field as naming the clinical context of malignancy association and must NOT read it as asserting that any individual keratosis becomes malignant; genuine malignant transformation of an individual keratosis is neither supported by the located evidence for this edge nor asserted by it.

Withheld routes and duplicate-scope screen: no skin-cancer edge (CATEGORY ERROR - the catalog skin-cancer identity denotes Melanoma / Non-Melanoma Skin Cancers, that is cutaneous malignancy, whereas the Leser-Trelat sign signals INTERNAL malignancy, so attaching this edge there would misstate the finding; the catalog cutaneous malignancy identities basal-cell-carcinoma and squamous-cell-carcinoma are the correct referents for any future evidence of genuine transformation, and both are left untouched by this batch); no basal-cell-carcinoma and no squamous-cell-carcinoma edge (EVIDENCE-INSUFFICIENT - genuine malignant transformation of an individual keratosis is rare, no anchor for it was located in this batch, and the located literature addresses the paraneoplastic sign rather than transformation); no pruritus edge (MISSING IDENTITY - the catalog carries only pruritus-ani, which is not the correct referent for generalised or localised keratosis-associated itch); and no visual-impairment edge (SCOPE - large or irritated eyelid keratoses can obstruct the visual axis, which would be a mechanical route, but no anchor for that specific claim was located in this batch and it is recorded here as a candidate for a future batch). This file is a sibling of seborrheic-dermatitis in skin-expansion-wave-6.json, but the two are genuinely distinct diseases, an inflammatory Malassezia-associated eruption and a benign epithelial tumour, so NO identity-duplication finding is recorded here.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: An abrupt eruptive onset of multiple seborrhoeic keratoses is the Leser-Trelat sign, a cutaneous paraneoplastic phenomenon whose most frequently reported underlying malignancies are gastrointestinal, and the located evidence frames it explicitly as an early-detection signal for colon cancer: a case report and review describes the Leser-Trelat syndrome as an UNDERDIAGNOSED cutaneous paraneoplastic syndrome that could aid in EARLY DETECTION OF COLON CANCER, and sets out the differential diagnoses, the completed workup, and current treatment options for a patient presenting with this pattern (PMID 37814771); a second case report documents the Leser-Trelat sign as an initial manifestation of synchronous prostate and bladder cancer, establishing the phenomenon as non-specific across tumour types rather than colon-specific (PMID 41158917); and a third case report documents the sign in a patient with gastric adenocarcinoma, supporting the gastrointestinal signal (PMID 37843094); recorded as a screening-signal association only, with the mechanism mismatch between the registered vocabulary and the paraneoplastic phenomenon disclosed on the face of the edge rather than resolved by inventing a category.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of colorectal cancer is established for any individual, and this edge asserts something materially weaker than a causal route: the located evidence supports the Leser-Trelat sign as a MARKER that may precede detection of an underlying internal malignancy, not a mechanism by which a keratosis produces cancer. The direction of the clinical arrow runs from the internal malignancy to the skin eruption, so the edge records the skin presentation as a possible screening signal and NOT as a cause of the tumour, and the reviewing clinician must understand that an individual claim on this basis would be a claim that the keratosis warrants a malignancy workup rather than a claim that the keratosis caused the cancer. The association is also substantially non-specific, as the located prostate and bladder case report shows, and the located evidence assembled for this edge is dominated by case reports and a descriptive clinical review rather than by a cohort, a systematic review, or a pooled estimate, so no frequency, no positive predictive value, and no incidence of malignancy in patients with eruptive keratoses can be quoted from these references. Individual claims require the documented eruptive onset with dated photographs or description, a malignancy workup with the results recorded, and an established cancer diagnosis independent of the skin finding.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The registered mechanism category is MALIGNANT_TRANSFORMATION and it is the closest available term in the controlled vocabulary, but the located evidence describes a PARANEOPLASTIC SIGNALLING route rather than transformation of the keratosis itself, and that mismatch is disclosed here rather than resolved by inventing a category outside the vocabulary: the hypothesised vector is that a tumour-derived secretory product or immune signal provokes abrupt proliferation of seborrhoeic keratoses in the skin, so the skin lesion is a downstream readout of an internal process rather than a transformed malignancy in its own right; a reviewer should therefore treat the mechanism field as naming the clinical context of malignancy association and NOT as asserting that any individual keratosis becomes malignant, and a separate and much rarer route, genuine malignant transformation of an individual keratosis into basal or squamous cell carcinoma, is neither supported by the located evidence for this edge nor asserted by it.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at case-report-and-review and case-report class, and registered as the file's sole edge because this identity is a benign epithelial tumour whose clinically important association is a paraneoplastic signal rather than a set of sequelae: the colon-cancer early-detection case report and review is the anchor that frames the sign as underdiagnosed and as an aid to early detection of colon cancer, which is the located basis for the target identity (PMID 37814771); the synchronous prostate and bladder case report is registered deliberately as evidence that the association is NON-SPECIFIC, so that the edge cannot be read as claiming a colon-specific route (PMID 41158917); and the gastric adenocarcinoma case report is registered as further support for the gastrointestinal signal (PMID 37843094). A descriptive clinical review of the sign (PMID 29244652) was located and reviewed but is not among this edge's three registered references because it is indexed in PubMed without abstract text, making it the weakest source class available for this association. Because the association is a non-specific screening signal rather than a causal route, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only, names the paraneoplastic framing, and discloses the mechanism-vocabulary mismatch explicitly.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The entire located evidence base for this edge is case reports, with no cohort, no case-control study, no systematic review, and no pooled estimate, so NO frequency, positive predictive value, or malignancy incidence in patients with eruptive keratoses can be quoted, and none is quoted; the case reports are by construction selected for diagnostic interest, particularly the synchronous prostate and bladder case which documents an unusual double tumour and therefore over-represents complexity; the sign is acknowledged in the broader literature as of uncertain and debated significance, and the located case report's own framing that the syndrome is UNDERDIAGNOSED implies the reported case base is incomplete; and no located anchor reports the base rate of eruptive seborrhoeic keratoses in patients WITHOUT malignancy, without which the positive predictive value of the sign cannot be estimated at all. A descriptive clinical review of the sign (PMID 29244652) was located and reviewed but is not registered because the three-reference cap applies and it is indexed without abstract text. Skin cancer as a target was reviewed and withheld as a CATEGORY ERROR: the catalog skin-cancer identity denotes Melanoma / Non-Melanoma Skin Cancers, that is cutaneous malignancy, whereas the Leser-Trelat sign signals internal malignancy, so attaching this edge to that identity would misstate the finding. Basal cell carcinoma was reviewed and withheld as EVIDENCE-INSUFFICIENT, since genuine transformation of an individual keratosis into basal cell carcinoma is rare and no anchor for it was located in this batch.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Non-specific internal malignancy of another site, which the located synchronous prostate and bladder case report documents directly and which means the sign cannot be attributed to colorectal disease without a workup

suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because an abrupt eruptive onset of multiple seborrhoeic keratoses is a recognised paraneoplastic sign whose most frequently reported underlying malignancies are gastrointestinal, and because the located evidence frames it explicitly as an underdiagnosed opportunity for early detection. The conservative framing states plainly that the edge records a screening signal rather than a causal route, registers the synchronous prostate and bladder case as positive evidence that the association is non-specific, discloses the mismatch between the registered mechanism category and the paraneoplastic phenomenon rather than inventing a vocabulary term, and withholds the cutaneous skin-cancer identity as a category error that would misstate the finding.

governanceNotes: D1 batch 82 (2026-09-27): one bounded association edge added - seborrheic-keratosis to colorectal-cancer (rank 1) at MALIGNANT_TRANSFORMATION, classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true. The edge records the Leser-Trelat sign, an abrupt eruptive onset of multiple seborrhoeic keratoses, as a PARANEOPLASTIC SCREENING SIGNAL for internal malignancy and expressly NOT as a causal route; the clinical arrow runs from the internal malignancy to the skin eruption. Anchors are the case report and review describing the syndrome as an underdiagnosed cutaneous paraneoplastic syndrome that could aid in early detection of colon cancer (PMID 37814771); the case report of the sign as an initial manifestation of synchronous prostate and bladder cancer, registered deliberately as evidence of NON-SPECIFICITY (PMID 41158917); and the case report of the sign in a patient with gastric adenocarcinoma (PMID 37843094). A descriptive clinical review of the sign (PMID 29244652) was located and reviewed but is not registered, the three-reference cap applying and that record being indexed without abstract text. The mechanism category is disclosed as a vocabulary compromise and must not be read as asserting malignant transformation of any individual keratosis. The catalog skin-cancer identity is withheld as a category error because it denotes cutaneous rather than internal malignancy.
